title: nf-core/rnaseq pipeline parameters
description: RNA sequencing analysis pipeline for gene/isoform quantification and extensive quality control.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to the sample sheet (CSV) containing metadata about the experimental samples.
input.help_text: Provide the full path to a comma-separated sample sheet with 4 columns and a header row. This file is required to run the pipeline. See the [nf-core/rnaseq sample sheet documentation](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq/usage#samplesheet-input) for example format.
input.errorMessage: The input must be a valid CSV file path with no spaces, ending in '.csv', and must exist.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Provide your email address to receive a summary report when the workflow completes. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`), you don't need to specify this for each run.
email.errorMessage: The email must be a valid address in the format 'name@example.com' and must not contain spaces.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

genome.description: Name of a `params.genomes` catalogue entry (iGenomes or a user-defined catalogue).
genome.errorMessage: The genome name must not contain spaces and must be a valid identifier.
genome.help_text: Selects a reference bundle from the `params.genomes` map and populates `fasta`, `gtf`, index paths, etc. from it. The pipeline ships the AWS iGenomes catalogue by default (entries like `--genome GRCh38`), but iGenomes annotations are vastly out of date and not recommended for new analyses. For modern reference data, supply `--fasta`/`--gtf` directly or define your own catalogue with the same `params.genomes` shape and load it via `-c`. See the [usage documentation](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq/usage#reference-catalogues-via---genome) for details.

fasta.help_text: This parameter is mandatory if `--genome` is not specified. If you don't have the appropriate alignment index, it will be generated automatically. Use with `--save_reference` to store the index for future runs.
fasta.errorMessage: The FASTA file path must end with .fa, .fna, .fasta optionally with .gz, must not contain spaces, and must exist.

gtf.help_text: This parameter is mandatory if `--genome` is not specified.
gtf.errorMessage: The GTF file must have a .gtf or .gtf.gz extension, must not contain spaces, and must exist.

gff.help_text: This parameter must be specified if neither `--genome` nor `--gtf` is provided.
gff.errorMessage: The GFF file must have a .gff, .gff3, .gff.gz, or .gff3.gz extension, must not contain spaces, and must exist.

gene_bed.description: Path to BED file containing gene intervals. This will be created from the GTF file if not specified.
gene_bed.errorMessage: The BED file must have a .bed or .bed.gz extension, must not contain spaces, and must exist.

transcript_fasta.help_text: If not provided, the transcriptome will be generated from the genome FASTA and GTF files. Cannot be used together with `--additional_fasta` when building a pseudo-aligner index, because the pipeline cannot append spike-in sequences to a user-provided transcriptome. Either omit this parameter or provide a pre-built index.

additional_fasta.description: FASTA file to concatenate to genome FASTA file e.g. containing spike-in sequences.
additional_fasta.help_text: If provided, sequences in this file will be concatenated to the genome FASTA file. A GTF file will be automatically created using these sequences, and alignment indices will be created from the combined files. Use `--save_reference` to reuse these indices in future runs. Cannot be used together with `--transcript_fasta` when building a pseudo-aligner index - either omit `--transcript_fasta` or provide a pre-built index that already contains the spike-ins.

splicesites.description: Splice sites file required for HISAT2.

star_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built STAR index.

hisat2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built HISAT2 index.

rsem_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built RSEM index.

salmon_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Salmon index.

kallisto_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Kallisto index.

bowtie2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Bowtie2 index.
bowtie2_index.help_text: Required when using `--aligner bowtie2_salmon`. If not provided, the index will be built from the transcript FASTA file for use with Salmon alignment-based quantification.

hisat2_build_memory.description: Minimum memory required to use splice sites and exons in the HiSAT2 index build process.
hisat2_build_memory.help_text: HiSAT2 requires significant RAM to build genome indices for large genomes with splice sites and exons (human genome typically needs 200GB). If you provide less memory than this threshold, splice sites and exons will be ignored, reducing memory requirements. For small genomes, set a lower value; for larger genomes, provide more memory.
hisat2_build_memory.errorMessage: Memory format must be a valid string like '200.GB', '16.MB', '8KB'.

gencode.description: Specify if your GTF annotation is in GENCODE format.
gencode.help_text: If your GTF file is in GENCODE format and you want to run Salmon (using `--pseudo_aligner salmon`), enable this parameter to build the Salmon index correctly.

prokaryotic.description: Enable prokaryotic mode for bacterial/archaeal RNA-seq data.
prokaryotic.help_text: Prokaryotic genomes have different annotation conventions than eukaryotes. This configures STAR to use CDS features instead of exons. Use `-profile prokaryotic` to enable this along with other recommended prokaryotic settings.

gffread_transcript_fasta.description: Use gffread to generate transcript FASTA instead of RSEM.
gffread_transcript_fasta.help_text: By default, RSEM is used to extract transcript sequences from the genome FASTA and GTF. RSEM expects exon features in the GTF, which may not be present in some annotations (e.g., prokaryotic). Enable this to use gffread instead, which handles CDS-only annotations correctly. This is automatically enabled by `-profile prokaryotic`.

gtf_extra_attributes.description: By default, the pipeline uses the `gene_name` field to obtain additional gene identifiers from the input GTF file when running Salmon.
gtf_extra_attributes.help_text: Modify this parameter to change which attributes are extracted from the GTF file when running Salmon. You can specify multiple values separated by commas (e.g., `--gtf_extra_attributes gene_id,transcript_id`).

gtf_group_features.description: Define the attribute type used to group features in the GTF file when running Salmon.

featurecounts_group_type.description: The attribute type used to group feature types in the GTF file when generating the biotype plot with featureCounts.

featurecounts_feature_type.description: By default, the pipeline assigns reads based on the 'exon' attribute within the GTF file.
featurecounts_feature_type.help_text: Specifies the feature type from the GTF file to use when generating the biotype plot with featureCounts.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Prevent loading of `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. Use this option if you encounter conflicts between custom parameters and those in the iGenomes configuration.

arm.help_text: Set automatically by the arm64 profile. Signals ARM architecture so that container closures can select ARM-compatible images where needed (e.g. STAR 2.6.1d in nf-test configs).

igenomes_base.description: The base path to the igenomes reference files

read_trimming_options.title: Read trimming options
read_trimming_options.description: Options to adjust read trimming criteria.

trimmer.description: Specifies the trimming tool to use - available options are 'trimgalore' and 'fastp'.

extra_trimgalore_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to Trim Galore! command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline. Only applicable when using `--trimmer trimgalore`.

extra_fastp_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to fastp command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline.

min_trimmed_reads.description: Minimum number of trimmed reads below which samples are removed from further processing. Some downstream steps in the pipeline will fail if this threshold is too low.

read_filtering_options.title: Read filtering options
read_filtering_options.description: Options for filtering reads prior to alignment

bbsplit_fasta_list.description: Path to comma-separated file containing a list of reference genomes to filter reads against with BBSplit. You have to also explicitly set `--skip_bbsplit false` if you want to use BBSplit.
bbsplit_fasta_list.help_text:
The file should contain 2 columns: short name and full path to reference genome(s), for example:
```
mm10,/path/to/mm10.fa
ecoli,/path/to/ecoli.fa
```

bbsplit_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built BBSplit index.
bbsplit_index.help_text: The BBSplit index must be built at least once with this pipeline. Use `--save_reference` to save the index, which can then be provided via `--bbsplit_index` for future runs.

sortmerna_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built sortmerna index.
sortmerna_index.help_text: The SortMeRNA index must be built at least once with this pipeline. Use `--save_reference` to save the index, which can then be provided via `--sortmerna_index` for future runs.

remove_ribo_rna.description: Enable the removal of reads derived from ribosomal RNA.
remove_ribo_rna.help_text: Any patterns found in sequences defined by the `--ribo_database_manifest` parameter will be used for filtering (when using SortMeRNA or Bowtie2).

ribo_removal_tool.description: Tool to use for rRNA removal.
ribo_removal_tool.help_text:
Choose between 'sortmerna' (default), 'bowtie2', or 'ribodetector' for rRNA removal.

- **sortmerna**: Reference-based filtering (default). Requires `--ribo_database_manifest`. Note: Default databases include SILVA sequences requiring licensing for commercial use.
- **bowtie2**: Alignment-based filtering. Requires `--ribo_database_manifest`. Recommended for users with SILVA licensing concerns as it supports custom databases.
- **ribodetector**: ML-based detection without a reference requirement. Useful for organisms lacking well-characterized rRNA sequences or to avoid database licensing requirements.

bowtie2_rrna_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Bowtie2 index for rRNA removal.
bowtie2_rrna_index.help_text: Optional when using `--remove_ribo_rna` and `--ribo_removal_tool` is set to `bowtie2`. If not provided, the index will be built using the database provided with `--ribo_database_manifest`

use_gpu_ribodetector.help_text: When enabled, ribodetector runs on GPU instead of CPU. Requires `--ribo_removal_tool ribodetector`. The ribodetector container includes both CPU and GPU binaries; the pipeline selects the GPU binary and requests one GPU accelerator when this option is set. Users needing multiple GPUs can override `accelerator` in their Nextflow config. Requires an NVIDIA GPU and appropriate container runtime flags, which are auto-detected (Docker: `--gpus all`, Singularity/Apptainer: `--nv`) or can be overridden via `--gpu_container_options`.

ribo_database_manifest.description: Text file containing paths to fasta files (one per line) that will be used to create the database for SortMeRNA.
ribo_database_manifest.help_text: By default, [rRNA databases](https://github.com/biocore/sortmerna/tree/master/data/rRNA_databases) from the SortMeRNA GitHub repository are used. See the example in `assets/rrna-default-dbs.txt`. Note: commercial/non-academic entities require [SILVA licensing](https://www.arb-silva.de/silva-license-information) for these databases.

umi_options.title: UMI options
umi_options.description: Options for processing reads with unique molecular identifiers

umi_dedup_tool.description: Specifies the tool to use for UMI deduplication - available options are 'umitools' and 'umicollapse'.

umitools_extract_method.description: UMI pattern to use. Can be either 'string' (default) or 'regex'.
umitools_extract_method.help_text: Detailed information can be found in the [UMI-tools documentation](https://umi-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/extract.html#extract-method).

umitools_bc_pattern.help_text: Detailed information can be found in the [UMI-tools documentation](https://umi-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/extract.html#extract-method).
umitools_bc_pattern.description: The UMI barcode pattern to use e.g. 'NNNNNN' indicates that the first 6 nucleotides of the read are from the UMI.

umitools_bc_pattern2.description: The UMI barcode pattern to use if the UMI is located in read 2.

umi_discard_read.description: After UMI barcode extraction discard either R1 or R2 by setting this parameter to 1 or 2, respectively.

umitools_umi_separator.errorMessage: The UMI separator must not contain spaces and must be a single character (e.g., ':').
umitools_umi_separator.description: The character that separates the UMI in the read name. Most likely a colon if you skipped the extraction with UMI-tools and used other software.

umitools_grouping_method.description: Method to use to determine read groups by subsuming those with similar UMIs. All methods start by identifying the reads with the same mapping position, but treat similar yet nonidentical UMIs differently.

umitools_dedup_stats.help_text: Generating these output statistics can be time-consuming. See [issue #827](https://github.com/nf-core/rnaseq/issues/827) for more information.
umitools_dedup_stats.description: Generate output stats when running "umi_tools dedup".

umitools_dedup_primary_only.description: Filter to primary alignments before UMI-tools dedup.
umitools_dedup_primary_only.help_text: When enabled, secondary and supplementary alignments (SAM flag 0x900) are removed before running UMI-tools dedup. This ensures dedup statistics reflect only primary alignments and are consistent with the rest of the QC flow (raw reads > trimmed > non-rRNA > aligned > deduplicated).

alignment_options.title: Alignment options
alignment_options.description: Options to adjust parameters and filtering criteria for read alignments.

aligner.description: Specifies the alignment algorithm to use - available options are 'star_salmon', 'star_rsem', 'hisat2', and 'bowtie2_salmon'.
aligner.help_text: Use 'bowtie2_salmon' for prokaryotic RNA-seq data. Bowtie2 is a splice-unaware aligner and is not recommended for eukaryotic data.

use_parabricks_star.description: Optionally accelerate STAR and MarkDuplicates with Parabricks

gpu_container_options.description: Override container GPU flags for GPU tasks. Auto-detects if not set (--gpus all for Docker, --nv for Singularity/Apptainer).

pseudo_aligner.description: Specifies the pseudo aligner to use - available options are 'salmon'. Runs in addition to '--aligner'.

pseudo_aligner_kmer_size.description: Kmer length passed to indexing step of pseudoaligners
pseudo_aligner_kmer_size.help_text: Setting an appropriate kmer size is crucial for quantification with Kallisto or Salmon. This is particularly important for short reads (<50bp), where the default size of 31 can cause problems.

bam_csi_index.description: Create a CSI index for BAM files instead of the traditional BAI index. This will be required for genomes with larger chromosome sizes.

star_ignore_sjdbgtf.description: When using pre-built STAR indices do not re-extract and use splice junctions from the GTF file.

salmon_quant_libtype.description: Override Salmon library type inferred based on strandedness defined in meta object.
salmon_quant_libtype.help_text: Refer to the [Salmon documentation](https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/library_type.html) for details on library types.

min_mapped_reads.description: Minimum percentage of uniquely mapped reads below which samples are removed from further processing.
min_mapped_reads.help_text: Samples below the threshold are left out of quantification (the aligner's merged count tables), duplicate marking, StringTie, featureCounts, bigWig and post-alignment QC, and are listed in the MultiQC report. They are still quantified by `--pseudo_aligner` if one is set. Downstream pipeline steps may fail if this threshold is set too low.

seq_center.description: Sequencing center information to be added to read group of BAM files.

seq_platform.description: Sequencing platform information to be added to read group of BAM files.

stringtie_ignore_gtf.description: Perform reference-guided de novo assembly of transcripts using StringTie i.e. dont restrict to those in GTF file.

extra_star_align_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to STAR alignment command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline. Only available for the STAR-Salmon route.

extra_hisat2_align_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to HISAT2 alignment command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline. Only available when using --aligner hisat2.

extra_bowtie2_align_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to Bowtie2 alignment command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline. Only available when using --aligner bowtie2_salmon.

extra_salmon_index_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to the Salmon index command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline.

extra_salmon_quant_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to Salmon quant command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline.

extra_kallisto_quant_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to Kallisto quant command in addition to defaults defined by the pipeline.

kallisto_quant_fraglen.description: In single-end mode Kallisto requires an estimated fragment length (in base pairs). Specify a default value for that here.

kallisto_quant_fraglen_sd.description: In single-end mode, Kallisto requires an estimated standard error for fragment length (in base pairs). Specify a default value for that here.

stranded_threshold.description: The fraction of stranded reads that must be assigned to a strandedness for confident assignment. Must be at least 0.5.

unstranded_threshold.description: The difference in fraction of stranded reads assigned to 'forward' and 'reverse' below which a sample is classified as 'unstranded'. By default the forward and reverse fractions must differ by less than 0.1 for the sample to be called as unstranded.

fail_on_low_trimmed_reads.description: Fail the run for samples with too few reads after trimming (see --min_trimmed_reads), instead of only skipping them.
fail_on_low_trimmed_reads.help_text: Failing samples are excluded from downstream steps and reported as a failed `SAMPLE_CHECK_FAILED` task, so the failure follows your `errorStrategy`. To let other samples finish and still exit with an error, set `process.errorStrategy = 'ignore'` and `workflow.failOnIgnore = true`.

fail_on_low_mapped_reads.description: Fail the run for samples with a mapping rate below --min_mapped_reads, instead of only skipping them.
fail_on_low_mapped_reads.help_text: Failing samples are excluded from downstream steps and reported as a failed `SAMPLE_CHECK_FAILED` task, so the failure follows your `errorStrategy`. To let other samples finish and still exit with an error, set `process.errorStrategy = 'ignore'` and `workflow.failOnIgnore = true`.

fail_on_undetermined_strandedness.description: Fail the run for samples with strandedness 'auto' that Salmon cannot determine, instead of treating them as 'unstranded'.
fail_on_undetermined_strandedness.help_text: Failing samples are excluded from downstream steps and reported as a failed `SAMPLE_CHECK_FAILED` task, so the failure follows your `errorStrategy`. To let other samples finish and still exit with an error, set `process.errorStrategy = 'ignore'` and `workflow.failOnIgnore = true`.

optional_outputs.title: Optional outputs
optional_outputs.description: Additional output files produces as intermediates that can be saved

save_merged_fastq.description: Save FastQ files after merging re-sequenced libraries in the results directory.

save_umi_intermeds.description: If this option is specified, intermediate FastQ and BAM files produced by UMI-tools are also saved in the results directory.

save_non_ribo_reads.description: If this option is specified, intermediate FastQ files containing non-rRNA reads will be saved in the results directory.

save_bbsplit_reads.description: If this option is specified, FastQ files split by reference will be saved in the results directory.

save_reference.description: If generated by the pipeline save the STAR index in the results directory.
save_reference.help_text: If the pipeline generates an alignment index, use this parameter to save it to your results folder for future pipeline runs, reducing processing time.

save_trimmed.description: Save the trimmed FastQ files in the results directory.
save_trimmed.help_text: By default, trimmed FastQ files are not saved. Enable this option to copy these files to the results directory.

save_align_intermeds.description: Save the intermediate BAM files from the alignment step.
save_align_intermeds.help_text: By default, only final filtered BAM files are saved to conserve storage. Enable this option to also save intermediate BAM files from the alignment process.

save_unaligned.description: Where possible, save unaligned reads from either STAR, HISAT2 or Salmon to the results directory.
save_unaligned.help_text: Output may be in FastQ or BAM format depending on the options available for the specific alignment tool used.

save_kraken_assignments.help_text: The `--kraken_db` parameter must be provided to use this option.

save_kraken_unassigned.description: Save reads that were not given assignment from Kraken2.
save_kraken_unassigned.help_text: The `--kraken_db` parameter must be provided to use this option.

extra_fqlint_args.description: Extra arguments to pass to the fq lint command.

deseq2_vst.description: Use vst transformation instead of rlog with DESeq2.
deseq2_vst.help_text: See the [DESeq2 documentation](http://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html#data-transformations-and-visualization) for details on transformations.

rseqc_modules.description: Comma-separated list of RSeQC modules to run.
rseqc_modules.help_text: Available modules include: bam_stat, inner_distance, infer_experiment, junction_annotation, junction_saturation, read_distribution, read_duplication, tin.
rseqc_modules.errorMessage: The RSeQC modules must be a comma-separated list of valid module names.

contaminant_screening.description: Tool to use for detecting contaminants in the selected screening reads - available options are 'sylph', 'kraken2', or 'kraken2_bracken'

contaminant_screening_input.description: Read set to screen for contaminants: aligner-unmapped reads (default), trimmed reads (post-BBSplit/rRNA), post-trim pre-BBSplit reads, or raw reads.
contaminant_screening_input.help_text: Use `unmapped` (default) to screen reads rejected by STAR/HISAT2 — requires alignment. Use `trimmed` to screen reads that passed BBSplit and rRNA filtering before alignment. Use `trim_only` to screen reads after adapter trimming but before BBSplit/rRNA removal — recommended when BBSplit removes expected contaminants. Use `raw` to screen pre-trimming reads (adapter sequences still present). `unmapped` requires `--aligner star_salmon`, `--aligner star_rsem`, or `--aligner hisat2`.

kraken_db.description: Database when using Kraken2/Bracken for contaminant screening.
kraken_db.help_text: See the usage documentation for more information on setting up and using Kraken2 databases. Requires the --contaminant_screening option to be set to 'kraken2' or 'kraken2_bracken' to have an effect

bracken_precision.description: Taxonomic level for Bracken abundance estimations.
bracken_precision.help_text: Use the first letter of taxonomic levels: Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, or Species. Requires --contaminant_screening option to be set to 'kraken2_bracken' to have an effect.

sylph_db.description: Comma separated list of databases to profile against when using Sylph for contamination detection
sylph_db.help_text: See the usage documentation for more information on setting up and using Sylph databases. Requires --contaminant_screening option to be set to 'sylph' to have an effect.

sylph_taxonomy.description: Comma separated list of taxonomies when using Sylph for contamination detection
sylph_taxonomy.help_text: See the usage documentation for more information on Sylph taxonomies. Requires --contaminant_screening option to be set to 'sylph' to have an effect.

process_skipping_options.title: Process skipping options
process_skipping_options.description: Options to skip various steps within the workflow.

skip_gtf_filter.description: Skip filtering of GTF for valid scaffolds and/ or transcript IDs.
skip_gtf_filter.help_text: If you're confident in your GTF file's compatibility with the genome FASTA file, or want to ignore filtering errors, enable this option.

skip_gtf_transcript_filter.description: Skip the 'transcript_id' checking component of the GTF filtering script used in the pipeline. Ensure the GTF file is valid.

skip_bbsplit.description: Skip BBSplit for removal of non-reference genome reads.

skip_umi_extract.description: Skip the UMI extraction from the read in case the UMIs have been moved to the headers in advance of the pipeline run.

skip_linting.description: Skip linting checks during FASTQ preprocessing and filtering.

skip_trimming.help_text: Use this option if your FastQ files have already been trimmed or if you're certain they contain no adapter contamination.

skip_alignment.description: Skip all of the alignment-based processes within the pipeline.

skip_pseudo_alignment.description: Skip all of the pseudoalignment-based processes within the pipeline.

skip_quantification_merge.description: Skip cross-sample count merging. Runs tximport per-sample instead of merged, producing individual gene/transcript-level TSVs per sample. Skips SummarizedExperiment and RSEM merge counts. Useful for very large cohorts.

use_rustqc.description: Experimental. Use RustQC instead of dupRadar, featureCounts biotype QC, RSeQC, Preseq, Qualimap, and samtools stats/flagstat/idxstats. Recommend trialling on pilot data first.

skip_dupradar.description: Skip dupRadar. Has no effect under `--use_rustqc` (experimental).

skip_qualimap.description: Skip Qualimap. Has no effect under `--use_rustqc` (experimental).

skip_rseqc.description: Skip RSeQC. Has no effect under `--use_rustqc` (experimental).

skip_biotype_qc.description: Skip additional featureCounts process for biotype QC. Has no effect under `--use_rustqc` (experimental).

skip_deseq2_qc.description: Skip DESeq2 PCA and heatmap plotting.

skip_qc.description: Skip all QC steps except for MultiQC.

differentialabundance_options.title: DA options
differentialabundance_options.description: Run nf-core/da on the merged gene counts generated by this workflow.

run_da.description: Run exploratory plots, differential plots, ShinyNGS, and Quarto reports after RNA-seq quantification.

da_input.description: DA sample metadata CSV/TSV containing the sample and design columns.

da_gtf.description: GTF used to annotate the RNA-seq count matrix.

da_features_gtf_feature_type.description: If a GTF file is supplied, which feature type to use

da_features_gtf_table_first_field.description: If a GTF file is supplied, which field should go first in the converted output table

da_gene_sets.description: Optional GMT gene-set database for functional analysis.

da_study_name.description: Study identifier used to name downstream outputs.

da_citations.description: Citations file used by the report.

da_shinyngs_deploy_to_shinyapps_io.description: Deploy the ShinyNGS application to shinyapps.io

da_shinyngs_shinyapps_app_name.description: The name of the app to push to in your shinyapps.io account

da_observations_id_col.description: Sample identifier column in the downstream metadata.

da_filtering_min_samples.description: Minimum observations that must pass the threshold to retain the row/ feature (e.g. gene).

da_filtering_min_proportion.description: A minimum proportion of observations, given as a number between 0 and 1, that must pass the threshold. Overrides  minimum_samples

da_filtering_grouping_var.help_text: The variable can be used to define groups and derive a minimum group size upon which to base minimum observation numbers. The rationale for this is to allow retention of features that might be present in only one group. Note that this is consciously NOT filtering with an explicit awareness of groups ("feature must be present in all samples of group A"), since this is known to create biases towards discovery of differential features.
da_filtering_grouping_var.description: An optional grouping variable to be used to calculate a min_samples value

da_filtering_min_proportion_not_na.description: A minimum proportion of observations, given as a number between 0 and 1, that must have a value (not NA) to retain the row/ feature (e.g. gene).

da_filtering_min_samples_not_na.description: Minimum observations that must have a value (not NA) to retain the row/ feature (e.g. gene). Overrides filtering_min_proportion_not_na.

da_exploratory_clustering_method.description: Clustering method used in dendrogram creation

da_exploratory_cor_method.description: Correlation method used in dendrogram creation

da_exploratory_n_features.description: Number of features selected before certain exploratory analyses. If -1, will use all features.

da_exploratory_whisker_distance.description: Length of the whiskers in boxplots as multiple of IQR. Defaults to 1.5.

da_exploratory_mad_threshold.help_text: MAD = median absolute deviation. A threshold on this value is used to define observations (samples) as outliers, or not, in exploratory plots. Based on the definition at https://archive.ph/o3thZ. For more on MAD, see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median_absolute_deviation.
da_exploratory_mad_threshold.description: Threshold on MAD score for outlier identification

da_exploratory_main_variable.description: How should the main grouping variable be selected? 'auto_pca', 'contrasts', or a valid column name from the observations table.
da_exploratory_main_variable.help_text: Some plots are only generated once, with a single sample grouping, this option defines how that sample grouping is selected. It should be 'auto_pca' (variable selected from the sample sheet with the most association with the first principal component), 'contrasts' (pick the variable associated with the first contrast), or a value specifying a specific column in the observations.

da_exploratory_assay_names.description: Specifies assay names to be used for matrices, platform-specific.

da_exploratory_final_assay.description: Specifies final assay to be used for exploratory analysis, platform-specific

da_exploratory_log2_assays.description: Of which assays to compute the log2 during exploratory analysis. Not necessary for maxquant data as this is controlled by the pipeline.
da_exploratory_log2_assays.help_text: Either comma-separated of assay positions, e.g. '[1,2,3]', or empty list '[]' to not log any assay. If not set, will guess which assays need to be logged (those with a maximum > 20).

da_exploratory_palette_name.help_text: Check the content of `RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info` from an R terminal for valid palette names or check [here](https://r-graph-gallery.com/38-rcolorbrewers-palettes.html).

da_differential_file_suffix.description: Advanced option: the suffix associated tabular differential results tables. Will by default use the appropriate suffix according to the study_type.

da_differential_feature_id_column.description: The feature identifier column in differential results tables

da_differential_min_fold_change.description: Minimum fold change used to calculate differential feature numbers. Note that this number will be log2 transformed

da_differential_max_pval.description: Maximum p value used to calculate differential feature numbers

da_differential_max_qval.description: Maximum q value used to calculate differential feature numbers

da_differential_palette_name.help_text: Check the content of `RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info` from an R terminal for valid palette names.

da_differential_subset_to_contrast_sampl.description: In differential analysis (DEseq2 or Limma), subset to the contrast samples before modelling variance?

da_deseq2_test.help_text: either "Wald" or "LRT", which will then use either Wald significance tests (defined by nbinomWaldTest), or the likelihood ratio test on the difference in deviance between a full and reduced model formula (defined by nbinomLRT)

da_deseq2_fit_type.help_text: either "parametric", "local", "mean", or "glmGamPoi" for the type of fitting of dispersions to the mean intensity. See estimateDispersions for description.

da_deseq2_sf_type.help_text: either "ratio", "poscounts", or "iterate" for the type of size factor estimation. See estimateSizeFactors for description.

da_deseq2_min_replicates_for_replace.help_text: the minimum number of replicates required in order to use replaceOutliers on a sample. If there are samples with so many replicates, the model will be refit after these replacing outliers, flagged by Cook's distance. Set to Inf in order to never replace outliers. It set to Inf for fitType="glmGamPoi".

da_deseq2_use_t.help_text: logical, passed to nbinomWaldTest, default is FALSE, where Wald statistics are assumed to follow a standard Normal

da_deseq2_independent_filtering.help_text: logical, whether independent filtering should be applied automatically

da_deseq2_lfc_threshold.help_text: a non-negative value which specifies a log2 fold change threshold. The default value is 0, corresponding to a test that the log2 fold changes are equal to zero. The user can specify the alternative hypothesis using the altHypothesis argument, which defaults to testing for log2 fold changes greater in absolute value than a given threshold. If lfcThreshold is specified, the results are for Wald tests, and LRT p-values will be overwritten.

da_deseq2_alt_hypothesis.help_text: character which specifies the alternative hypothesis, i.e. those values of log2 fold change which the user is interested in finding. The complement of this set of values is the null hypothesis which will be tested. If the log2 fold change specified by 'name' or by contrast' is written as beta , then the possible values for 'altHypothesis' represent the following alternate hypotheses: 1) greaterAbs: |beta| > lfcThreshold , and p-values are two-tailed 2) lessAbs: |beta| < lfcThreshold , p-values are the maximum of the upper and lower tests. The Wald statistic given is positive, an SE-scaled distance from the closest boundary 3) greater: beta > lfcThreshold 4) less: beta < -lfcThreshold

da_deseq2_p_adjust_method.help_text: the method to use for adjusting p-values, see help in R for the p.adjust() function (via ?p.adjust). At time of writing available values were "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BH", "BY", "fdr", "null".

da_deseq2_alpha.help_text: the significance cutoff used for optimizing the independent filtering (by default 0.1). If the adjusted p-value cutoff (FDR) will be a value other than 0.1, alpha should be set to that value.

da_deseq2_minmu.help_text: lower bound on the estimated count (used when calculating contrasts)

da_deseq2_vs_method.description: variance stabilisation method to use when making a variance stabilised matrix

da_deseq2_shrink_lfc.help_text: 'ashr' method is the only method currently implemented

da_deseq2_vs_blind.description: `blind` parameter for rlog() and/ or vst()
da_deseq2_vs_blind.help_text: logical, whether to blind the transformation to the experimental design

da_deseq2_vst_nsub.help_text: the number of genes to subset to (default 1000)

da_gsea_permute.help_text: Select the type of permutation to perform in assessing the statistical significance of the enrichment score. (See 'required fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page for more info)

da_gsea_nperm.help_text: Specify the number of permutations to perform in assessing the statistical significance of the enrichment score. (See 'required fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page)

da_gsea_scoring_scheme.help_text: See 'basic fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page for a detailed explanation.

da_gsea_sort.help_text:
GSEA ranks the genes in the expression dataset and then analyzes that ranked list of genes. Use this parameter to determine whether to sort the genes using the real (default) or absolute value of the ranking metric.

See 'basic fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page

da_gsea_order.help_text:
GSEA ranks the genes in the expression dataset and then analyzes that ranked list of genes. Use this parameter to determine whether to sort the genes in descending (default) or ascending order. Ascending order is usually applicable when the ranking metric is a measure of nearness (how close the genes are to one another) rather than distance.

See 'basic fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page

da_gsea_set_max.help_text:
After filtering from the gene sets any gene not in the expression dataset, gene sets larger than this are excluded from the analysis.

See 'basic fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page

da_gsea_set_min.help_text:
After filtering from the gene sets any gene not in the expression dataset, gene sets smaller than this are excluded from the analysis.

See 'basic fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page

da_gsea_norm.help_text:
Normalization mode. Method used to normalize the enrichment scores across analyzed gene sets: 'meandiv' (default, GSEA normalizes the enrichment scores as described in Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)) OR 'null' (GSEA does not normalize the enrichment scores).

See 'advanced fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page

da_gsea_rnd_type.help_text:
Method used to randomly assign phenotype labels to samples for phenotype permutations. Not used for gene_set  permutations.

See 'advanced fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page

da_gsea_median.help_text:
Set to true (default=false) to use the median of each class, instead of the mean, in the metrics for ranking for genes

See 'advanced fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page.

da_gsea_num.help_text:
Number of features (gene or probes) to include in the butterfly plot in the Gene Markers section of the gene set enrichment report.

See 'advanced fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page.

da_gsea_plot_top_x.description: Plot graphs for the top sets of each phenotype
da_gsea_plot_top_x.help_text:
Generates summary plots and detailed analysis results for the top x genes in each phenotype, where x is 20 by default. The top genes are those with the largest normalized enrichment scores.

See 'advanced fields' at https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/doc/GSEAUserGuideFrame.html?Run_GSEA_Page.

da_gsea_save_rnd_lists.help_text: Set to 'true' (default=false) to save the random ranked lists of genes created by phenotype permutations. When you save random ranked lists, for each permutation, GSEA saves the rank metric score for each gene (the score used to position the gene in the ranked list). Saving random ranked lists is memory intensive; therefore, this parameter is set to false by default.

da_gsea_zip_report.description: Make a zipped file with all reports
da_gsea_zip_report.help_text: Set to True (default=false) to create a zip file of the analysis results. The zip file is saved to the output folder with all of the other files generated by the analysis. This is useful for sharing analysis results

da_gprofiler2_organism.description: Short name of the organism that is analyzed, e.g. hsapiens for homo sapiens.
da_gprofiler2_organism.help_text: Set this to the [short organism name](https://biit.cs.ut.ee/gprofiler/page/organism-list) consisting of the first letter of the genus and the full species name, e.g. hsapiens for Homo sapiens, mmusculus for Mus musculus. This has second priority and will be overridden by --gprofiler2_token.

da_gprofiler2_significant.description: Should only significant enrichment results be considered?
da_gprofiler2_significant.help_text: Default true; if false, will consider all enrichment results regardless of significance.

da_gprofiler2_measure_underrepresentatio.description: Should underrepresentation be measured instead of overrepresentation?
da_gprofiler2_measure_underrepresentatio.help_text: Default false; if true, will measure overrepresentation.

da_gprofiler2_correction_method.description: The method that should be used for multiple testing correction.
da_gprofiler2_correction_method.help_text: One of gSCS (synonyms: analytical, g_SCS), fdr (synonyms: false_discovery_rate), bonferroni.

da_gprofiler2_sources.description: On which source databases to run the gprofiler query
da_gprofiler2_sources.help_text: GO, GO:MF, GO:BP, GO:CC, KEGG, REAC, WP, TF, MIRNA, HPA, CORUM, HP, or any comma-reparated combination thereof, e.g. 'KEGG,REAC'. This works if --gprofiler2_organism is used; if a GMT file is provided with --gene_sets_files, should also work; the module will then remove any lines not starting with any of the source names. Does not work for --gprofiler2_token as g:Profiler will not filter such a run.

da_gprofiler2_evcodes.description: Whether to include evcodes in the results.
da_gprofiler2_evcodes.help_text: This can decrease performance and make the query slower. See https://rdrr.io/cran/gprofiler2/man/gost.html

da_gprofiler2_max_qval.description: Maximum q value used for significance testing.

da_gprofiler2_token.description: Token that should be used as a query.
da_gprofiler2_token.help_text: For reproducibility, instead of querying the online databases, you can provide a token, e.g. from a previous pipeline run or from a manual query on https://biit.cs.ut.ee/gprofiler/gost. This has highest priority and will override --gprofiler2_organism and --gene_sets_files.

da_gprofiler2_background_file.description: Path to CSV/TSV/TXT file that should be used as a background list of genes for the query; alternatively, 'auto' (default) or 'false'.
da_gprofiler2_background_file.help_text: It is advisable to run pathway analysis with a set of background genes describing which genes exist in the target organism in the first place so that other genes are not at all considered. This parameter is by default set to 'auto', meaning that the filtered input abundance matrix will be used. Alternatively, you can provide a CSV/TSV table where one column contains gene IDs and the other rows contain abundance values, or a TXT file that simply contains one gene ID per line. If a custom CSV/TSV is used, all genes will be considered which had at least some abundance (i.e. sum of all abundance values in a row > 0). Set to 'false' if you do not want to use a background.

da_gprofiler2_background_column.description: Which column to use as gene IDs in the background matrix.
da_gprofiler2_background_column.help_text: If a background matrix is provided but this parameter is not set, will assume that the first matrix column contains the IDs.

da_gprofiler2_domain_scope.description: How to calculate the statistical domain size.
da_gprofiler2_domain_scope.help_text: One of annotated (default), known, custom or custom_annotated; see https://rdrr.io/cran/gprofiler2/man/gost.html

da_gprofiler2_min_diff.description: How many genes must be differentially expressed in a pathway for it to be considered enriched? Default 1.

da_gprofiler2_palette_name.help_text: Check the content of `RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info` from an R terminal for valid palette names.

da_decoupler_network.description: Path to TSV file containing network file for decoupler

da_decoupler_min_n.description: Removes sources of a net with less than min_n targets

da_decoupler_methods.description: Comma-separated list of methods to use (e.g., 'ora,ulm')

da_grea_set_min.description: Minimum number of features in a gene set.

da_grea_set_max.description: Maximum number of features in a gene set.

da_grea_permutation.description: Number of permutations used by grea to estimate enrichment significance.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: These parameters define centralized configuration profiles that appear in the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You typically don't need to modify these values.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: When running offline, Nextflow cannot retrieve institutional configuration files from the internet. If needed, download these files from the repository and specify their location with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text: These options are common across all nf-core pipelines and control core pipeline behavior. Typically set in a Nextflow config file (e.g., `~/.nextflow/config`) for all pipeline runs.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: Controls how files are saved to the output directory through Nextflow's `publishDir` directive. See the [Nextflow documentation](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for available options.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: Specify an email address to receive a summary report only when the pipeline fails to complete successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

force_completion_email.description: Send the completion email on Seqera Platform launches, where it is skipped by default.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename.
trace_report_suffix.help_text: You can use '{date}' as a placeholder which will be replaced with the current date and time in the format 'yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss'. For example, 'run_{date}' will become 'run_2023-05-15_14-30-45'.
trace_report_suffix.errorMessage: The trace report suffix must only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, hyphens, dots, and curly braces for date placeholders.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
